summary: Katsumi Okimoto is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a graduate student at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1973). He served at Hanazono University as a professor (~1980–2008) and later as director (~2008).

Katsutoshi Ono was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1928–1931). He served on the faculty at Ryukoku University (~1960–1976) and Kansai University (~1976–1981).
Kavita Singh was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. She completed her studies at Lady Shri Ram College for Women (~1982–1985) and Panjab University (~1985–1987).

Kazi Dawa Samdup was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who served as headmaster at Maharaja's Bhutia Boarding School (~1906–1919) and teacher at the University of Calcutta (~1919–1922). He taught Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz and Herbert Bruce Hannah.
Kazu Uehara was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyushu University. He later served as professor emeritus at Seijo University (~1995–2017).
Kazuaki Komine is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Tokushima University (~1980–1990) and later served as professor emeritus at Rikkyo University (attested 2015–2019).

Kazufumi Oki is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University. He taught Shinshu Kusumoto and held positions as assistant professor (attested 1982–1988) and professor emeritus (attested 2006–2013) at Shuchiin University.

Kazuharu Mizuno studied at Nagoya University (BA, ~1978–1982), Hokkaido University (Master's, ~1982–1984), and Tokyo Metropolitan University (DSc, ~1985–1990). He served as professor of geography in the Graduate School of Letters at Kyoto University (~2009).

Kazuhiko Yoshida is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Sophia University, Kyoto University, and Cornell University (PhD), studying under Jay Jasanoff. He held posts at Nagoya City University (~1987–1992) and Kyoto University as professor (~1999–2020).
Kazuhiro Furuta is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as dean at Otani University (attested 1998) and was an editor and publisher at the Otani Society (attested 1991).
Kazuhiro Kawasaki is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at Koyasan University (~2000–2005) and served there as a researcher (attested 2005).
Kazuhiro Yamamoto is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Silpakorn University under doctoral supervisors Samniang Leurmsai and Chirapat Prapandvidya (attested 2009).

Kazunobu Matsuda, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied as a graduate student at Otani University. He held positions at Otani University, Kyoto University, and Bukkyo University (professor, 2009), and taught Shintaro Kitano and Ikko Arai.

Kazuo Hyodo is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under Hajime Sakurabe at Otani University (PhD). He served as an assistant professor at Otani University (~1984–2014) and on the Otani Society committee.

Kazuo Kano studied at Kyoto University (MA under Katsumi Mimaki) and the University of Hamburg (PhD under David P. Jackson and Klaus-Dieter Mathes). A scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held posts at Hamburg, Kyoto, Koyasan, and Komazawa.
Kazuo Okabe is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at Komazawa University (~1954–1958). He served as a professor at Komazawa University (~1980–2005) and taught Jamie Hubbard.

Kazuo Osumi was a scholar of history, archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1955). He held posts at Hokkaido University (~1968–1982) and Tokyo Woman's Christian University as professor (~1982–2002).
Kazuo Oyamada is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Tamagawa University (~1971–1975) and held a post at Rissho University.

Kazuyoshi Hotta is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007). He held posts at the University of Tokyo Young Buddhist Association (attested 2007) and Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. Educated at Shudo Junior & Senior High School and the University of Tokyo (~1945–1948), he held posts at Shogen Junior College and Hosen Gakuen College.
